prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “best” broker for every self‑employed person — the right broker depends on your budget, health needs, whether you want ACA/marketplace coverage, an HSA plan, short‑term coverage, or a small‑group/association solution. That said, look for an independent, Missouri‑licensed broker with strong experience serving self‑employed/sole‑proprietor clients.

How to choose a good broker in Kansas City, MO
- Use an independent broker who can compare multiple carriers (not a captive agent tied to one insurer).  
- Verify they’re licensed in Missouri (Missouri Dept. of Insurance producer lookup).  
- Prefer brokers who regularly help self‑employed clients and know ACA marketplace rules, HSA plans, QSEHRA/ICHRA, and association/group options.  
- Ask about fees (most broker commissions are paid by carriers but ask if they charge client fees), enrollment support, year‑round service, and tax/benefits guidance.  
- Read Google/Yelp/Better Business Bureau reviews and ask for local references.

Types of brokers/agencies worth contacting
- Large national brokers with local KC offices (can handle complex cases): HUB International, Arthur J. Gallagher, Alera Group / USI (check local office availability).  
- Local independent brokers and small agencies — often more hands‑on and good for individual/self‑employed cases. Find them via Google (“independent health insurance broker Kansas City”), NAHU’s Find An Agent tool, or the Missouri Dept. of Insurance.  
- Online marketplaces (if you prefer self‑service plus broker support): eHealth or HealthSherpa — they let you compare ACA plans quickly and connect you to licensed agents.

Questions to ask any broker before you commit
- How many self‑employed/sole‑proprietor clients do you work with?  
- Which carriers and plan types do you represent? Are you independent?  
- Will you help enroll me in the ACA marketplace and handle renewals/changes?  
- Do you charge client fees or are you paid by carriers?  
- Can you help with HSAs, COBRA, QSEHRA/ICHRA, or small‑group alternatives if that becomes an option?  
- Can you provide references from Kansas City clients?

Next step I can do for you
If you want, tell me your ZIP code, whether you need individual or family coverage, and any must‑haves (HSA, low deductible, specific doctors), and I’ll find 2–3 Kansas City brokers or agencies that match your needs and summarize their strengths.
